overview:
All five main statements follow from one: $L(s,\chi)\neq0$ for every Dirichlet character $\chi$ and every $s$ with $\operatorname{Re}s>1/2$, except at the pole of $\zeta$. The functional equation handles the strip and the Riemann Hypothesis itself, and the finitely many Euler factors that separate an imprimitive character from its primitive one do not vanish for $\operatorname{Re}s>0$. So the work is to prove the half-plane statement for a primitive character $\psi$.

For $\psi$ the argument considers the cyclic group of characters generated by $\psi$ and a positive combination $G_\psi(x)$ of the sums $\sum_{n\le x}\Lambda(n)\chi(n)(x/n-1)$ over that group, corrected by their main terms $x\log x$ and $x\frac{L'}{L}(1,\chi)$. A quantitative form of Landau's theorem shows that a one-sided bound $G_\psi(x)\le x^{1/2+O(\varepsilon)}$, known only on windows $[Y,Y^{3/2}]$ for arbitrarily large $Y$, already excludes zeros with $\operatorname{Re}s>1/2+O(\varepsilon)$; the positivity it uses is that a real zero contributes a pole with positive residue. At each scale $x$ the window bound is proved inside an abelian CM host field: the compositum of the layer of degree about $x^{2+8\varepsilon}$ of the $2$-power cyclotomic tower, the field of $\psi$, and $\mathbf Q(\sqrt{-q},\sqrt{-d})$ for auxiliary primes of size $\exp(x^{\varepsilon/5})$. The primes are chosen, using zero-density estimates and mean values over quadratic twists, so that all other characters of the host field have square-root cancellation at the relevant scales, and Behrend's construction gives a large set of Frobenius classes without short relations.

The window bound comes from a descendant of Stepanov's method. An exact identity, proved by orthogonality of the characters of the host field, rewrites $G_\psi$ in terms of the difference between a sum over primes $p$ inert in the host field, $\sum_p2\log p\sum_i(a/p^{i}-w)_+$, and a main term $a(\log a-1-\gamma+\cdots)$. The inequality "inert-prime sum $\le$ main term $+$ error" is obtained by measuring one auxiliary Hermitian lattice in two ways. The lattice consists of automorphic forms obtained by lifting an algebraic modular form along a chain of totally definite unitary groups $U(X_0)\subset U(X_1)\subset\cdots\subset U(X_m)$ by explicit theta kernels, $\pi\mapsto\pi\boxplus\mu_1[t+1]\boxplus\cdots\boxplus\mu_m[t+1]$, with $m$ about $\sqrt x$, glued across tuples $\mu$ of Hecke characters. From below, the periods of the $m$-fold lift, which equal Bessel periods by a seesaw argument, are divisible at each inert prime by about $a/p+a/p^{3}+\cdots$ per lift, coming from $p$-integrality of theta functions on CM elliptic curves; this replaces multiplicity, and a frame form of Bost's slope inequality turns it into a lower bound for the slope of the lattice, using near-orthogonality of its columns (Siegel-Weil and Poincaré series) and Green's description of cuspidal characters of $GL_d(\mathbf F_g)$. From above, an arithmetic volume estimate on toroidal compactifications of unitary Shimura varieties bounds its covolume, through a flat-degree formula that uses the Chowla-Selberg formula in its $\eta$ form. The mass formula enters that bound too, as the identity between volume and mass of Gan-Hanke-Yu and Prasad, which bounds the volume of each level subgroup; a rank-one case of Siegel's formula supplies the volume ratio inside its proof. Siegel's mass-ratio theorem and the Rallis inner product formula enter on the definite side instead, where the mass ratios bound how the class counts grow along the chain and so guide the choice of families.

The local error terms at the places where the characters are twisted are controlled by Tate-Shafarevich groups of Tate twists over the host field, and the argument needs $\sum_\ell\log\ell\sum_{k<x^{401}}\operatorname{len}\text{Ш}^1(E,\mathbf Q_\ell/\mathbf Z_\ell(-k))\le e^{x^{\varepsilon}/2}$ on most windows of scales. This weakening of Vandiver's conjecture is proved by bounding the minus part with an Euler system of Gauss sums, the plus part with Eisenstein congruences on residually reducible deformation rings for $U(3)$ and $GSp_4$ shown to be automorphic, and the prime $2$ with the Ferrero-Washington theorem, Iwasawa theory in the $2$-power tower and a bound of Soulé type on $K$-theoretic cohomology.

The argument draws on about one hundred and fifty results from the literature, among them Galois representations attached to polarized cuspidal representations of $GL_n$ over CM fields, a local Langlands correspondence for $GL_n$, the Siegel-Weil formula, Howe duality, base change for unitary groups, Bhatt-Scholze's crystalline lattices and resolution of singularities. All of them are proved, several in forms weaker than the published theorems that suffice for the places where they are used.
